# screenmat

> A local-first tool that turns a raw screenshot into a shareable visual:
> rounded window frame, generative background derived from the screenshot's own
> colours, annotations, redaction, multi-shot compositions, high-resolution
> export. No backend, no account, no network call. The same rendering engine is
> reachable from a Node API, a CLI, and an MCP server — that second door is what
> this documentation covers.

Everything below is Markdown, served as-is. Fetch a page to read it in full, or
concatenate all eight for the complete reference (roughly 2000 lines).

## Docs

- [Overview](/docs/overview.md): what the machine door is, requirements, a
  60-second quickstart in all three modes, and which settings each façade can
  reach.
- [CLI](/docs/cli.md): the four command forms, every flag with its default and
  bounds, output paths, the `--json` result shape, exit codes and error messages.
- [MCP server](/docs/mcp.md): how to register the server, the write guard
  (`SCREENMAT_OUT`, never overwrites), and the three tools — `screenmat_render`,
  `screenmat_inspect`, `screenmat_list_styles` — with their full parameters.
- [Node API](/docs/api.md): `render(spec)` and `inspect(input, settings)`,
  their result types, and the errors they throw.
- [Scene format](/docs/scene.md): the complete serialisable JSON — settings,
  composition, shots, layers, watermark, palette — every field with its default
  and its bounds, plus how validation clamps rather than rejects.
- [Coordinates](/docs/coordinates.md): the layer coordinate frame. Read this
  before placing any annotation: rects are fractions of the **window width**,
  `y` included, and `w`/`h` are signed.
- [Styles](/docs/styles.md): tune once in the app, export a `.json`, drop it in
  `~/.screenmat/styles/`, recall it by name. Precedence and caching.
- [Recipes](/docs/recipes.md): runnable examples — batch, device frames,
  deterministic backgrounds, redaction, annotations, compositions, Playwright —
  followed by a troubleshooting list.

## Optional

- [Web app](/): the human door. Four screens — Edit, Batch, Styles, History —
  and the place where a style is created in the first place.
